mappingScope: Fixed-Go source obligations and nearby test intent, not a direct luac-equivalence claim. Go v3.2.0 has LuaLS Runtime.Check, not this Rust bundled luac component. Existing Rust public typed errors remain the direct compatibility baseline for this narrow ownership repair.

mappings.scope: Validate/admit before process entry; fresh scratch is owned by one call. Pre-run failures and an empty/no-process request can clean only their owned directory. Rust keeps its existing deadline code/message/exit and legacy best-effort removal semantics.

The owning process layer must retire a started child/tree. This caller does not infer retirement from an error or metadata. The new tests model that caller boundary, plus one real rejected-spawn path; they do not replace the existing actual Windows process-tree tests.

mappings.go: internal/luals/runtime.go:Runtime.Check runGuarded error projection and completed result processing
mappings.scope: Keep selected public errors and distinguish compiler nonzero status from runner failure. A returned Output at status 0 or 1 is terminal for scratch ownership; diagnostic interpretation remains unchanged.

strongerRetentionDifference.go: Runtime.Check unconditionally defers frozenWorkspace cleanup after setup; frozenWorkspace cleanup calls os.RemoveAll(dir) best-effort. Go has no analogous retained-owner receipt in this path.
strongerRetentionDifference.rust: After either Rust runner has been entered, every Err retains scratch even if spawn never started a child or all diagnostic cleanup flags are true. Ordinary return adds the existing retained-scratch marker and receipt without changing code/message/exit; publication failure appends cleanup detail. Panic propagates and leaves scratch without claiming a receipt. Only an Ok(Output) rearms cleanup.
strongerRetentionDifference.reason: Do not delete while process, exact Job or pipe workers may still own the directory. This is an explicit conservative ownership extension already used by the ordered Rust path, not a Go behavioral-parity pass.

ci.command: node tools/rust-cargo.mjs --owner ci-ordered-luac --one-shot -- test --locked --offline -p lycheedev-source --lib luac::ordered_tests -j 1

notCovered: No Rust/Cargo type checking or unit execution in this batch. The independently reviewed local pure harness currently admits only its fixed raw_json/mailbox tests; it was not expanded or bypassed.
No Windows Job, worker, process retirement, native input or game execution.
No guarantee of hard real-time filesystem finalization or checked legacy cleanup: pre-run and post-success best-effort Drop behavior is intentionally preserved.
This patch neither changes the process candidate nor proves its terminal-output contract; that three-file candidate remains a separately frozen/reviewed dependency.
